main_text.l: sustinens? Deinde sicut aer non impedit casum seu
motum aquæ: ita verisimile non est, ab aqua impe-
diri motum terræ, maximè cum quantum aqua pon-

perat aquam. Postremò, palàm uidemus, exiguam
terræ portionem, si in aquam proijciatur, statim
moueri, & ima petere: quid ni igitur eodem modo

3.[?] Anaximanes, Anaxagoras & Democritus ter-
ræ motu prohiberi opinabantur, propter amplam
eius latitudinem æquatamq; superficiem: hanc enim
tantam esse, ut aerem circumpositum diuidere nul-
lo modo possit. Aere autem nulla ex parte diuiso, quo
moueatur terra? Sed neque aer potest loco cedere,
utpote non habens quo se recipiat: quare nec terra
aliquem aeris locum subire valet. Eadem autem
ratione uidemus, in vasculū, cui unum tantum sit exi-
guum foramen, non ingredi aquam, quòd nimirum
aer inclusus, qui nusquam potest egredi, obsistat.

page.notes: The first paragraph continues from the previous page. The numerals "2." and "3." at the paragraph openings are printed in an italic form that I read as 2 and 3; please check them. The gathering signature at the foot is hard to read and is given as "o 5" with a doubt mark. The printed "Empe-" / "docles" break has no hyphen at the line end, so the word is written whole. Printed u for v (uanam, uerisimile, uidemus, uasculū, etc.) was corrected to v, as the rules require. The word "vasculū" carries a tilde over the final u as printed.
